statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39824 (GO-2026-5024): NewNTUnicodeString in golang.org/x/sys/windows did not check for length overflow, so a string longer than an NTUnicodeString can describe (a 16-bit byte count) gave a truncated string instead of an error. It is fixed in golang.org/x/sys v0.44.0 by commit fb1facd (CL 770080, which names CVE-2026-39824): https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5024, https://go.dev/issue/78916, https://go.dev/cl/770080, https://github.com/golang/sys/commit/fb1facd76f95fa87c151018200ea5e4892ff115d, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/6MMI8Lj-Atg. The Go vulnerability database lists the vulnerable symbol as golang.org/x/sys/windows NewNTUnicodeString on GOOS windows only, and the fix's only change outside tests is to windows/syscall_windows.go, a file Go compiles only for Windows targets. Debian lists its golang-golang-x-sys package as not affected: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-39824. We read every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 33 builds, 0.20.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r5, each for x86_64 and aarch64 and each matching its repository index checksum. Each package holds a single file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a Linux program (its Go build information records GOOS=linux) that lists golang.org/x/sys at v0.38.0 to v0.49.0 depending on the build. In no build do its Go function table or its ELF symbol table contain a golang.org/x/sys/windows function or a NewNTUnicodeString name, and a byte search of every build finds neither name; as a control, the same function-table reader finds golang.org/x/sys/unix and golang.org/x/sys/cpu functions in the 0.24.0-r5 x86_64 binaries of external-dns and external-dns-fips, and runtime.main in every build. The vulnerable Windows-only package is not compiled into these Linux builds.

CVE-2026-39824 (GO-2026-5024): NewNTUnicodeString in the golang.org/x/sys/windows package before golang.org/x/sys 0.44.0 does not check for length overflow, and returns a truncated string instead of an error when the input is longer than an NTUnicodeString's 16-bit byte length can hold: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5024 and https://github.com/golang/go/issues/78916. The Go vulnerability database limits it to that package on Windows (goos windows, symbol NewNTUnicodeString), and the fix, https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/sys/+/770080, changes only windows/syscall_windows.go and its test. The golang.org/x/sys/windows package is built only for Windows: a program importing it with golang.org/x/sys v0.43.0 fails to build for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 with 'build constraints exclude all Go files'. The vulnerable code is not in this package. We downloaded every package built from the metrics-server source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: metrics-server and metrics-server-dev from the main repository and metrics-server-fips and metrics-server-fips-dev from the security repository, each 0.8.1-r0 through the current 0.9.1-r2 (29 builds), for x86_64 and aarch64, 232 package files, each checked against its repository index checksum and data hash. Each holds one file and no symbolic links: /usr/bin/metrics-server, a statically linked Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0, with no module replacements. Its build information lists golang.org/x/sys v0.40.0 to v0.50.0 (v0.45.0 or later from 0.8.1-r9). The Go function table of every build contains functions of golang.org/x/sys/unix and none of golang.org/x/sys/windows, and a byte search of every binary finds no golang.org/x/sys/windows, NewNTUnicodeString or NTUnicodeString string while finding golang.org/x/sys/unix. in each; the same reader finds runtime.main in every build. As a positive control, the same program built for windows/amd64 contains golang.org/x/sys/windows.NewNTUnicodeString (go tool nm).
